subject: physics
question_text: How do AI and machine learning help scientists in astrophysics?

Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the gravitational-wave detection and galaxy-shape classification examples are real, published applications of machine learning in astrophysics.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The method
lines: AI and machine learning search very large
telescope and detector data sets, faster
than a person can search by eye.
They pick out weak signals hidden in noise.
steps.why: Telescope and detector surveys record data sets far too large for a person to search by eye, so a trained model finds the patterns instead.
common_mistakes: Writing only that AI is used, without saying it searches large data sets faster than a person.
Naming a completely unrelated task instead of searching data for weak signals.
steps.memory_tip: AI searches faster: large data sets, weak signals, found by a trained model.
steps.margin_note: Both the speed point and the weak-signal point help earn this mark in full.

steps.label: The example
lines: Also used to sort galaxies by shape.
steps.why: Gravitational-wave detection and galaxy-shape sorting are real, published examples of machine learning used in astrophysics.
common_mistakes: Giving a vague example such as 'space research' without naming a specific use.
Naming an example from a different field, such as medicine.
steps.memory_tip: Remember one concrete example: gravitational waves from merging black holes.
steps.margin_note: Any one correctly described example earns this mark.
